text.text_excerpt: I feel like it's maybe a little strange to review a grocery store? (What, you don't know what a Whole Foods is?) But: I work in Mid City, so this place has become my go-to for quick office lunches and grabbing groceries on my way home, so I think I've got some good stuff to share. 1. Their coffee is SO GOOD and so cheap! Plus a great selection of pastries from local bakeries. It saves me a trip to a cafe is I also need to grab something else. 2. Their bulk food is great, and makes it easy to stock up on dry goods. 3. $5 and under cheese bin, a magical trove of wonders that won't break your bank. 4. Their prepared food/salad bar isn't totallllly bank breaking, but maybe not the cheapest in...

I live in the Marigny/Bywater area, and until this place opened, I'd have to trek out to Metairie or across town to the Arabella store to get the stuff that only Whole Foods sells locally. It was okay, but not great. Now that the Broad St. store opened, I'm only 10 minutes away, and I love it. I also love the fact that it's smaller. I just get overwhelmed going into a store for a couple of specific items and feeling like I have to stretch first to make my way through the aisles and aisles of stuff. It's not quite as cool as the old Whole Foods on Esplanade was, but it's a lot better than the massive one in Metairie for sure, and way less pretentious than the one uptown! It actually feels ...

As I live in Mid-City, I've been excited about this Whole Foods ever since they started building it. Now I can avoid the long drive uptown and literally walk a few blocks down to this Whole Foods. Upon visiting on the grand opening day, there were so many people that I thought I was going to die of too many people overload, but that most likely won't be the case as time continues on. The parking lot is rather small however, for a Whole Foods, so a word of advice: park on the street right next to the parking lot. Not only will you find a spot, but you'll exit much easier and faster. For the quality of the store itself, see my review for the uptown Whole Foods. Everything is really the same...
